plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.8
plan.contextChunk: This figure titled Some Familiar Solids of Revolution shows four side-by-side pairs (a)-(d), each consisting of a 2D plane region and the 3D solid it generates when revolved about an axis of revolution. Panel (a): a rectangle revolves to produce a right circular cylinder. Panel (b): a semicircle revolves to produce a solid sphere. Panel (c): a right triangle revolves to produce a solid cone. Panel (d): a rectangle separated from the axis revolves to produce a hollowed right circular cylinder. Each pair shows the 2D region at top with the axis of revolution marked as a horizontal line and a rotation arrow, and the resulting 3D solid below. The figure catalogs familiar 3D solids as examples of solids of revolution, motivating the general method of computing volumes by revolving a plane region about an axis.

elements: Text label 'Axis of revolution' beneath the axis
Curved rotation arrow around the right end of the axis
2D generating region in the XY plane (light cyan with dark border)
3D swept solid volume (translucent cyan, updating dynamically with the revolution angle)
Label indicating the name of the current solid

interactions.label: Solid Type
interactions.teaches: Selects the 2D generating plane region, demonstrating that different standard shapes result from revolving different profiles.

interactions.label: Revolution angle (deg)
interactions.teaches: Sweeps the 2D region continuously around the axis, making the rotational generation of the 3D volume directly visible.
Allows inspection of the 3D solid from all angles, revealing interior structures like the empty core of the hollowed cylinder.

demo_steps.title: Cylinder Revolution
demo_steps.narration: A rectangle resting on the axis revolves fully to form a solid right circular cylinder.

demo_steps.title: Generating a Sphere
demo_steps.narration: A semicircle revolves around its diameter. Sweeping 180 degrees shows the hemisphere mid-formation.

demo_steps.title: Inside the Cone
demo_steps.narration: A right triangle revolves to form a cone. A partial sweep reveals the 2D triangular generator inside the volume.

demo_steps.title: Hollowed Cylinder
demo_steps.narration: A rectangle separated from the axis leaves a cylindrical void in the center as it revolves, forming a tube.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axis of revolution: line along X-axis from X=-3 to X=3. 2D regions lie in the XY plane (Z=0, Y > 0) with length spanning X=-2 to X=2 and max height Y=1.5. Cylinder: rectangle Y=0 to 1.5. Sphere: semicircle centered at origin, radius 1.5. Cone: right triangle with vertices at (-2,0), (2,0), and (2,1.5). Hollowed cylinder: rectangle offset from axis, Y=0.6 to 1.5. Colors: 2D region fill #bfe6eb, border #008b8b; 3D solid #3fb4c1 at 0.65 opacity. Include a curved arrow (arc + arrowhead) around the X-axis at X=2.6 in the YZ plane.
interactionPlan.notes: Use LatheGeometry (or similar procedural sweep) around the X-axis to generate the 3D solid dynamically based on the sweepAngle slider. Render the solid as double-sided and semi-transparent so the internal 2D generating region remains visible. When sweepAngle < 360, cap the two cut planes (at 0 and at the current angle) so the partial solid appears as a closed volumetric slice.

authoredContext: A solid of revolution is a solid that is generated by revolving a plane region about a line that lies in the same plane as the region; the line is called the axis of revolution. Many familiar solids are of this type (Figure 5.2.8).
